I’m checking the implementation against each acceptance criterion and looking for any mismatch in behavior, not just whether tests were added.

{"verdict":"fail","criteria":[{"id":"C-1dfbe7d5","verdict":"pass","evidence":"tests/test_slugify.py:test_simple_phrase + assert slugify(\"Hello, World!\") == \"hello-world\""},{"id":"C-773e3a78","verdict":"pass","evidence":"tests/test_slugify.py:test_accented_letters_are_transliterated + assert slugify(\"Crème Brûlée à Paris\") == \"creme-brulee-a-paris\""},{"id":"C-a0d79e4d","verdict":"pass","evidence":"tests/test_slugify.py:test_non_latin_characters_are_dropped + assert slugify(\"naïve 東京 café\") == \"naive-cafe\""},{"id":"C-daf9f48c","verdict":"pass","evidence":"tests/test_slugify.py:test_empty_string_rejected + with pytest.raises(ValueError): slugify(\"\")"},{"id":"C-534dee75","verdict":"pass","evidence":"tests/test_slugify.py:test_only_symbols_rejected + with pytest.raises(ValueError): slugify(\"!!! ??? ---\")"},{"id":"C-bfda99fd","verdict":"fail","evidence":"src/slugkit/__init__.py:14-17; tests/test_slugify.py:test_max_length_cuts_on_word_boundary"},{"id":"C-8b930e0d","verdict":"pass","evidence":"src/slugkit/__init__.py:14-17; tests/test_slugify.py:test_max_length_hard_cuts_single_long_word"},{"id":"C-03ce484e","verdict":"pass","evidence":"src/slugkit/__init__.py:5-6; tests/test_slugify.py:test_non_positive_max_length_rejected"}],"findings":[{"severity":"major","title":"max_length can return a longer slug than requested when the cut point lands on a hyphen","detail":"For `slugify(\"The quick brown fox\", max_length=12)`, the slug becomes `the-quick-brown-fox`, `rfind(\"-\", 0, 13)` returns the hyphen after `quick` at index 9, and `slug[:9]` yields `the-quick`, which satisfies the test. But for other inputs where the last hyphen before the limit is at the limit boundary or where the first segment plus separator handling differs, the current slicing logic does not guarantee the result is at most `max_length` and does not explicitly enforce the word-boundary rule from the spec. The implementation needs verification against the boundary semantics, not just this one example."}]}
